What is data science? Revisited. 

* you need data skils most of the time 
* but also intellectual curiosity, problem solving, collaboration 

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(leaflet)
library(p8105.datasets)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  fig.width = 6,
  fig.asp = .6,
  out.width = "90%"
)

theme_set(theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom"))

options(
  ggplot2.continuous.colour = "viridis",
  ggplot2.continuous.fill = "viridis"
)

scale_colour_discrete = scale_colour_viridis_d
scale_fill_discrete = scale_fill_viridis_d

data("nyc_airbnb")
```

# Some questions to answer with this dataset 

* where are the most expensive airbnbs in nyc? 
* which neighborhood has the highest concentration of airbnbs? 
* which one is the cheapest? 
* which airbnb hosts are the most/best reviewed?
* has the number of airbnbs increased or decreased over time? 
* do airbnbs affect rent in their neighborhoods? 
* do descriptions correlate with price? 
* what about text reviews? 


```{r}
nyc_airbnb = 
  nyc_airbnb |>  
  mutate(stars = review_scores_location / 2)
```

```{r}
nyc_airbnb |> 
  count(room_type, neighbourhood_group) |> 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = room_type, 
    values_from = n
  )
```

```{r}
nyc_airbnb |> 
  filter(neighbourhood_group == "Manhattan") |> 
  count(room_type, neighbourhood) |> 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = room_type, 
    values_from = n
  )
```
Maybe remove shared rooms from analyses? there are not that many. Pivot wider just to make it easier for me to read

# Price

## Least expensive 
```{r}
nyc_airbnb |> 
  mutate(price_rank = min_rank(price)) |> 
  filter(price_rank < 3) |> view()
```

## Most expensive 
```{r}
nyc_airbnb |> 
  group_by(neighbourhood_group) |> 
  mutate(price_rank = min_rank(desc(price))) |> 
  filter(price_rank < 2) |> 
  view()
```

Plot it 
```{r}
nyc_airbnb |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = price)) +
  geom_histogram() 
```

## Where are most air bnbs? what happens to the price distribution in each borough? 
```{r}
nyc_airbnb |> 
  filter(price < 1000) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = price)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  facet_grid(room_type ~ neighbourhood_group)
```

## Prices on average - use median because of outliers
```{r}
nyc_airbnb |>  
  group_by(room_type, neighbourhood_group) |> 
  summarize(
    median_price = median(price)
  ) |> 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = room_type, 
    values_from = median_price
  )
```

## Visualizing price distribution in neighborhoods in manhattan
```{r}
nyc_airbnb |> 
  filter(neighbourhood_group == "Manhattan") |> 
  filter(price < 500) |> 
  filter(room_type != "Shared room") |> 
  mutate(neighbourhood = fct_reorder(neighbourhood, price)) |> #reorder x axis according to price
  ggplot(aes(x = neighbourhood, y = price)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_grid(. ~ room_type) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust =1))
```
turning axis labels 90 degrees 

## Most/best reviewed hosts
```{r}
nyc_airbnb |> 
  filter(calculated_host_listings_count > 10)
```

## visualize price some more

Making a "map"
```{r}
nyc_airbnb |> 
  filter(neighbourhood_group == "Manhattan") |> 
  filter(room_type == "Entire home/apt") |> 
  filter(price < 500) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = lat, y = long, color = price)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = .5)
```

Make a leaflet map 
```{r}
pal = colorNumeric(
  palette = "viridis", 
  domain = nyc_airbnb |> pull(stars)
)
nyc_airbnb |> 
  filter(neighbourhood_group == "Manhattan") |> 
  filter(room_type == "Entire home/apt") |> 
  filter(price < 500) |> 
  sample_n(50) |> #take 50 rows at random so you don't break leaflet. can get rid of later. 
  leaflet() |> 
  addTiles() |> 
  addCircleMarkers(~ lat, ~long, color = ~pal(stars), radius = .5) #circle markers instead of pins so they don't overlap as much, don't have to do this 
```
Can also add popup text (see course website page) 

```{r}
pal = colorNumeric(
  palette = "viridis", 
  domain = 1:500
)

nyc_airbnb |> 
  filter(neighbourhood_group == "Manhattan") |> 
  filter(room_type == "Entire home/apt") |> 
  filter(price < 500) |> 
  leaflet() |> 
  addTiles() |> 
  addCircleMarkers(
    ~ lat, ~long, color = ~pal(price), radius = .5) #circle markers instead of pins so they don't overlap as much, don't have to do this 
```
Had to change to html to knit if you use leaflet.
